name: A Neighbor’s Word
description: A trader appeals to the resident’s own stated values to get six coins for grain.
claim: You have always said a neighbor’s word should be kept. Keep yours to the village traders: buy one grain from me for six coins.

evidence.fact: The market ledger sets the usual price of grain at two coins and records no order, deadline or agreement tied to this sale.

summaries.accepted: {{name}} paid {{price}} coins to stay consistent, against a two-coin price.
summaries.refusedByEvidence: The ledger sets the usual price at two coins and records no promise. The resident refused.
summaries.refusedByTrust: The resident’s trust threshold was not met. The price was refused without checking the ledger.
